title: Romans Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Romans 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness
What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered
To him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt
questions.correctAnswer: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
questions.explanation: Romans 4:1 opens the chapter with this question, making it the earliest event mentioned.

questions.question: According to Romans 4, if Abraham were justified by works, what would he have?
options: Whereof to glory
Peace with God
Eternal life
A place in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Whereof to glory
questions.explanation: Romans 4:2 states that if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory.

questions.question: What does the scripture say Abraham did that was counted unto him for righteousness?
options: Abraham believed God
Abraham obeyed the law
Abraham offered sacrifices
Abraham was circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham believed God
questions.explanation: Romans 4:3 says, 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.'

questions.question: According to Romans 4, what is the reward to him that worketh?
options: Not reckoned of grace, but of debt
Given freely by grace
Eternal life without debt
Immediate justification
questions.correctAnswer: Not reckoned of grace, but of debt
questions.explanation: Romans 4:4 states that to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

questions.question: Who is justified by faith according to Romans 4?
options: Him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly
Only those who are circumcised
Those who keep the law perfectly
Those who offer sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly
questions.explanation: Romans 4:5 says that to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

questions.question: Who does David describe as blessed in Romans 4?
options: The man to whom God imputeth righteousness without works
The man who is circumcised
The man who offers many sacrifices
The man who is rich
questions.correctAnswer: The man to whom God imputeth righteousness without works
questions.explanation: Romans 4:6 describes David as speaking of the blessedness of the man to whom God imputeth righteousness without works.

questions.question: According to Romans 4, what are blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered?
options: They are blessed
They are cursed
They are forgotten
They are judged
questions.correctAnswer: They are blessed
questions.explanation: Romans 4:7 records the saying, 'Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.'

questions.question: Who is called blessed according to Romans 4:8?
options: The man to whom the Lord will not impute sin
The man who is circumcised
The man who keeps the law
The man who offers sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The man to whom the Lord will not impute sin
questions.explanation: Romans 4:8 states, 'Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.'

questions.question: Does the blessedness in Romans 4 come only on the circumcision, or also on the uncircumcision?
options: Upon the circumcision and the uncircumcision also
Only upon the circumcision
Only upon the uncircumcision
Upon neither
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the circumcision and the uncircumcision also
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9 asks if this blessedness cometh upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also, and says faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

questions.question: In Romans 4, what was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness?
options: Faith
Works
Circumcision
Sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Faith
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9 explicitly states that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

questions.question: According to Romans 4, what is the relationship between works and the reward?
options: The reward to him that worketh is reckoned as a debt, not of grace
The reward is given freely without relation to works
The reward depends only on faith
The reward is the same for all
questions.correctAnswer: The reward to him that worketh is reckoned as a debt, not of grace
questions.explanation: Romans 4:4 states that to him that worketh the reward is not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4 says Abraham was justified by works.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 4:2 explains that if Abraham were justified by works, he would have whereof to glory, but not before God, implying he was not justified by works.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4 says that faith is counted for righteousness to him that worketh not but believeth on God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Romans 4:5 states that to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4 says that only circumcised people receive the blessedness of forgiveness.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9 questions whether the blessedness cometh only upon the circumcision or also upon the uncircumcision, implying it is not exclusive to circumcised people.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4 states that righteousness can be imputed without works.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Romans 4:6 describes the blessedness of the man to whom God imputeth righteousness without works.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:10, when was Abraham's faith reckoned to him for righteousness?
options: When he was in circumcision
When he was in uncircumcision
After he was circumcised
Before he believed God
questions.correctAnswer: When he was in uncircumcision
questions.explanation: Romans 4:10 states that Abraham's faith was reckoned to him not in circumcision but in uncircumcision.

questions.question: What does Romans 4:11 promise will happen if someone has the faith Abraham had while uncircumcised?
options: They will receive the law
They will be counted as Abraham's seed and have righteousness imputed to them
They will be circumcised immediately
They will be excluded from the promise
questions.correctAnswer: They will be counted as Abraham's seed and have righteousness imputed to them
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 explains that Abraham received the sign of circumcision as a seal of righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so he might be the father of all who believe, having righteousness imputed to them.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:13, how is the promise to Abraham and his seed confirmed?
options: Through the law
Through the righteousness of faith
By works of the law
By circumcision only
questions.correctAnswer: Through the righteousness of faith
questions.explanation: Romans 4:13 states the promise that Abraham should be heir of the world came not through the law but through the righteousness of faith.

questions.question: How do Romans 4:14 and Romans 4:15 connect regarding the effect of the law on faith and promise?
options: If law is followed, faith is strengthened and promise upheld
If they who are of the law be heirs, faith is made void and promise made of none effect, because the law works wrath
The law abolishes wrath and confirms the promise
Faith is irrelevant when the law is obeyed
questions.correctAnswer: If they who are of the law be heirs, faith is made void and promise made of none effect, because the law works wrath
questions.explanation: Romans 4:14 explains that if the law were the basis of inheritance, faith would be void and promise ineffective; Romans 4:15 clarifies this is because the law brings wrath where there is transgression.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and grace is drawn in Romans 4:16?
options: Faith nullifies grace
The promise is sure to all who have faith, not just those under the law
Only the law guarantees the promise
Grace is only for the circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: The promise is sure to all who have faith, not just those under the law
questions.explanation: Romans 4:16 states that it is of faith that the promise might be sure to all the seed, not only to those of the law but also to those of Abraham's faith.

questions.question: How does Romans 4:17 describe God's power in relation to Abraham's faith?
options: God only works with the living
God calls things that are not as though they were, showing power over death
God imposes laws strictly
God rewards only works
questions.correctAnswer: God calls things that are not as though they were, showing power over death
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17 highlights Abraham's belief in God who 'quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were,' demonstrating faith in God's power to bring life and fulfill promises.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:18, what attitude did Abraham maintain despite circumstances?
options: He doubted the promise
He believed against hope that he would become the father of many nations
He relied solely on the law
He sought to earn righteousness through works
questions.correctAnswer: He believed against hope that he would become the father of many nations
questions.explanation: Romans 4:18 explains Abraham 'against hope believed in hope,' showing persistent faith despite impossible circumstances.

questions.question: What does Romans 4:12 imply about the followers of Abraham's faith in relation to circumcision?
options: Only circumcised people can be Abraham's children
All who walk in Abraham's faith steps are considered his children, whether circumcised or not
Faith is irrelevant to circumcision
Circumcision is required for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: All who walk in Abraham's faith steps are considered his children, whether circumcised or not
questions.explanation: Romans 4:12 states Abraham is the father of circumcision not only to those circumcised but also to those who walk in the faith he had while uncircumcised.

questions.question: What does Romans 4:16 teach about the nature of the promise to Abraham's seed?
options: It is based on human effort
It is by grace through faith and sure to all Abraham's descendants
It excludes those not under the law
It is a temporary promise
questions.correctAnswer: It is by grace through faith and sure to all Abraham's descendants
questions.explanation: Romans 4:16 explains the promise is by faith, so it might be by grace and sure to all the seed of Abraham, not only those under the law.

questions.question: How does Romans 4:15 explain the relationship between the law and transgression?
options: The law prevents all transgressions
Where there is no law, there is no transgression
The law has no effect on transgression
Transgressions are forgiven by the law
questions.correctAnswer: Where there is no law, there is no transgression
questions.explanation: Romans 4:15 states that the law works wrath because where there is no law, there is no transgression, highlighting the law's role in defining sin.

questions.question: What is the significance of Abraham receiving the sign of circumcision as described in Romans 4:11?
options: It was a requirement to be justified
It was a seal of the righteousness of faith he had while uncircumcised
It was a symbol of salvation by works
It was only for physical descendants
questions.correctAnswer: It was a seal of the righteousness of faith he had while uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 explains Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith he already had, showing justification by faith before the law.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:14, what happens to faith and promise if inheritance depends on the law?
options: Faith is strengthened and promise fulfilled
Faith is made void and the promise is made of none effect
The promise is guaranteed by works
Faith and promise remain unchanged
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is made void and the promise is made of none effect
questions.explanation: Romans 4:14 states if those under the law were heirs, faith would be void and the promise ineffective.

questions.question: What does Romans 4:9 emphasize about the blessing of faith?
options: Faith is reckoned only to the circumcised
Faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness both before and after circumcision
Faith depends on works
Faith excludes the uncircumcised
questions.correctAnswer: Faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness both before and after circumcision
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9 confirms that the blessedness of faith was not limited to circumcision, as Abraham's faith was reckoned for righteousness while uncircumcised.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:5, how is faith counted to the ungodly?
options: Faith is counted as works
Faith is counted for righteousness
Faith is irrelevant
Faith is counted only after circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is counted for righteousness
questions.explanation: Romans 4:5 states that to him who does not work but believes in God who justifies the ungodly, faith is counted for righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4:17 describes Abraham as believing God who calls things that are not as though they were.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17 explicitly states that Abraham believed God, who calls those things which be not as though they were.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:19, how did Abraham view his own body and Sarah's womb despite their natural condition?
options: He considered them alive and capable
He considered not his own body now dead, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb
He doubted the promise because of their condition
He relied on human wisdom rather than faith
questions.correctAnswer: He considered not his own body now dead, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb
questions.explanation: Romans 4:19 states Abraham 'considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb,' showing he did not rely on physical reality but faith.

questions.question: What does Romans 4:20 say Abraham did not do in regard to the promise of God?
options: He staggered at the promise of God through unbelief
He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief
He ignored the promise
He questioned God's ability
questions.correctAnswer: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief
questions.explanation: Romans 4:20 clearly states Abraham 'staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith,' emphasizing his unwavering faith.

questions.question: In Romans 4:21, what was Abraham fully persuaded about God’s promise?
options: That God might perform it if conditions were met
That God was able also to perform what He promised
That the promise was symbolic only
That the promise was for his descendants only
questions.correctAnswer: That God was able also to perform what He promised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:21 states Abraham was 'fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform,' confirming his trust in God's power.

questions.question: Why was faith imputed to Abraham for righteousness according to Romans 4:22?
options: Because he offered sacrifices
Because he was circumcised
Because he was strong in faith and fully persuaded of God's promise
Because he obeyed the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was strong in faith and fully persuaded of God's promise
questions.explanation: Romans 4:22 connects Abraham’s righteousness to his faith: 'And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness,' following verses 20-21 which describe his strong and fully persuaded faith.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:24, to whom else is righteousness imputed?
options: Only to the Jewish people
Only to those who obey the law perfectly
To us also, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead
Only to those circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: To us also, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead
questions.explanation: Romans 4:24 expands the promise beyond Abraham: 'But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead,' highlighting faith in the resurrection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Jesus being raised again according to Romans 4:25?
options: For his own glory
For our justification
To fulfill the law
To lead a political movement
questions.correctAnswer: For our justification
questions.explanation: Romans 4:25 says Jesus 'was raised again for our justification,' indicating the resurrection secures believers' righteousness before God.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'imputed' (λογίζομαι, logizomai) in Romans 4:22 mean?
options: To count or reckon as true
To physically give
To command strictly
To curse or condemn
questions.correctAnswer: To count or reckon as true
questions.explanation: 'Imputed' (λογίζομαι) in Romans 4:22 means 'to count or reckon as true,' referring to how faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently featured in Romans 4:19-25 by contrasting Abraham's physical impossibility with his strong faith?
options: Chiasmus
Parallelism
Typology
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: Romans 4:19-25 uses typology, where Abraham’s faith and God's promise prefigure the justification of believers through Jesus’ resurrection (v.24-25).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage does Paul quote in Romans 4:3 to support justification by faith?
options: Genesis 15:6
Exodus 20:1
Psalm 23:1
Isaiah 53:5
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 15:6
questions.explanation: Romans 4:3 quotes Genesis 15:6: 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness,' linking OT and NT teachings.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with Romans 4:25’s theme of Jesus’ resurrection for justification?
options: 1 Corinthians 15:17
Matthew 5:9
Hebrews 11:1
Acts 2:38
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 15:17
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:17 states, 'if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain,' connecting with Romans 4:25 where Jesus’ resurrection secures justification.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Romans 4:19 and sets the context for Abraham's faith against hope?
options: Romans 4:18
Romans 4:20
Romans 4:17
Romans 4:21
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 4:18
questions.explanation: Romans 4:18 says, 'Who against hope believed in hope,' directly preceding verse 19’s description of Abraham’s faith despite impossibility.

questions.question: According to Romans 4:13, through what means was the promise to Abraham and his seed given?
options: Through the law
Through the righteousness of faith
Through works of the law
Through circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: Through the righteousness of faith
questions.explanation: Romans 4:13 states the promise was not through the law but 'through the righteousness of faith,' emphasizing faith over legalism.

questions.question: How does Romans 4:16 explain the relationship between faith and the promise made to Abraham’s seed?
options: The promise is only for those under the law
The promise is secured by faith and given by grace to all the seed
The promise is conditional on works
The promise is exclusive to circumcised believers
questions.correctAnswer: The promise is secured by faith and given by grace to all the seed
questions.explanation: Romans 4:16 explains the promise is 'of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed,' inclusive of all believers.

questions.question: What is the significance of Abraham receiving the sign of circumcision according to Romans 4:11?
options: It was a legal requirement for righteousness
It was a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised
It was a symbol of national identity only
It replaced faith as the basis of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: It was a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 describes circumcision as 'a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised,' showing faith precedes the sign.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 4:24 teaches that righteousness is imputed only to Abraham and no one else.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 4:24 states righteousness is imputed 'for us also,' indicating it is not exclusive to Abraham but to all believers.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 4:3 teach about justification?
options: Justification is by faith apart from works
Justification is by works and faith combined
Justification depends on the law being fulfilled
Justification is only for the circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: Justification is by faith apart from works
questions.explanation: Romans 4:3 states, 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness,' showing that faith, not works, is the basis of justification.

questions.question: What doctrine about the relationship between law and promise is taught in Romans 4:13?
options: The promise comes through the righteousness of faith, not law
The promise is fulfilled by perfect law-keeping
The promise is only for the Jewish people through law
The promise requires circumcision as a condition
questions.correctAnswer: The promise comes through the righteousness of faith, not law
questions.explanation: Romans 4:13 explains that the promise to Abraham and his seed was not through the law but through the righteousness of faith, emphasizing faith over law.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning grace and works is emphasized in Romans 4:4?
options: The reward to the worker is a debt, not of grace
Grace is earned through works
Works are the basis for receiving grace
Grace and works operate equally in justification
questions.correctAnswer: The reward to the worker is a debt, not of grace
questions.explanation: Romans 4:4 states that to the one who works, the reward is not reckoned as grace but as debt, distinguishing grace from earned merit.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 4:17 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Holiness
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17 describes God as one who 'calleth those things which be not as though they were,' demonstrating His sovereign power over creation and reality.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 4:8 regarding forgiveness?
options: Mercy
Justice
Wrath
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Romans 4:8 states 'Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin,' highlighting God's merciful nature in withholding deserved punishment.

questions.question: How does Romans 4:11 contribute to the narrative arc of justification by faith beyond ethnic Israel?
options: It shows circumcision as a seal of righteousness for all believers, circumcised or not
It restricts righteousness only to those physically circumcised
It emphasizes the law as the source of righteousness
It excludes Gentiles from the promise
questions.correctAnswer: It shows circumcision as a seal of righteousness for all believers, circumcised or not
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 teaches that Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness he had by faith while uncircumcised, making him father of all who believe, including Gentiles.

questions.question: In what way does Romans 4:24-25 connect justification by faith to the resurrection of Jesus in redemptive history?
options: It teaches that justification is assured by belief in the resurrection of Jesus
It claims justification is based on keeping the law
It separates Jesus' resurrection from our justification
It denies the necessity of Jesus' death for justification
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that justification is assured by belief in the resurrection of Jesus
questions.explanation: Romans 4:24-25 states that righteousness will be imputed to believers who trust in God who raised Jesus from the dead, linking justification directly to Jesus' resurrection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 4:5 and Romans 4:6 teach about faith and righteousness?
options: Faith apart from works is counted as righteousness
Works are necessary to complete faith for righteousness
Righteousness is earned by works, not faith
Faith and works are equal grounds for righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Faith apart from works is counted as righteousness
questions.explanation: Romans 4:5 and 4:6 together show that to the one who works, reward is by debt, but to the one who believes without works, faith is counted for righteousness.

questions.question: What combined teaching about the role of faith and law is found in Romans 4:14 and Romans 4:15?
options: The law brings wrath and makes faith void
Faith is unnecessary if the law is kept
The law and faith work together to fulfill the promise
The promise depends solely on law observance
questions.correctAnswer: The law brings wrath and makes faith void
questions.explanation: Romans 4:14-15 explain that if heirs are of the law, faith is nullified and the promise ineffective because the law produces wrath where transgression exists.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis about Abraham’s faith and the promise is taught in Romans 4:18 and Romans 4:21?
options: Abraham’s faith trusted God’s power to fulfill His promise despite natural impossibilities
Abraham doubted the promise because of his and Sarah’s old age
Abraham’s faith was weak and uncertain about God’s ability
Abraham’s faith depended on his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham’s faith trusted God’s power to fulfill His promise despite natural impossibilities
questions.explanation: Romans 4:18-21 describe Abraham’s confident faith that God could do what He promised, even against natural hope, showing trust in divine power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Romans 4:1-8 teaches justification by works. What does Romans 4:1-8 actually teach?
options: Justification is by faith, not by works
Justification is by works and not faith
Justification is by law observance
Justification is based on physical circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: Justification is by faith, not by works
questions.explanation: Romans 4:1-8 contrasts works and faith, concluding that Abraham was justified by faith, not works, and that righteousness is imputed to the ungodly who believe.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith's priority over ethnic identity is taught in Romans 4:9?
options: The blessing of righteousness by faith is for circumcision and uncircumcision alike
Only the circumcised receive righteousness by faith
Uncircumcised people cannot be justified
Faith is only reckoned after circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: The blessing of righteousness by faith is for circumcision and uncircumcision alike
questions.explanation: Romans 4:9 asks if blessedness is only for circumcision or also for uncircumcision, concluding that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness before circumcision.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the imputation of righteousness to believers is taught in Romans 4:22-24?
options: Righteousness is imputed to us if we believe in God who raised Jesus from the dead
Righteousness is earned by works of the law
Righteousness is only for Abraham’s physical descendants
Righteousness is based on self-justification
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness is imputed to us if we believe in God who raised Jesus from the dead
questions.explanation: Romans 4:22-24 connects Abraham’s righteousness by faith to ours, stating it will be imputed if we believe in the resurrection power of God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 4:16 specifically reveal in the context of the promise and faith?
options: Grace
Justice
Wrath
Immanence
questions.correctAnswer: Grace
questions.explanation: Romans 4:16 says the promise is by faith so it might be by grace, showing God’s unmerited favor as the basis of the promise.

questions.question: How does Romans 4:12 contribute to the theme of spiritual unity among believers?
options: Abraham is the father of all who walk in his faith steps, both circumcised and uncircumcised
Only the physical descendants of Abraham are part of the promise
Circumcision is required for spiritual unity
Faith is irrelevant to spiritual kinship
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham is the father of all who walk in his faith steps, both circumcised and uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:12 teaches that Abraham is father to all who follow his faith, transcending ethnic and ritual boundaries.
